quizzes.title: Mercator Projection: Shape, Size and Grid
quizzes.passage: Turning the round surface of the Earth into a flat map always involves some distortion. Different projections handle this in different ways, and the Mercator design is one of the most familiar. On the Mercator grid, longitudes are evenly spaced, but the gaps between latitudes widen as one moves towards the Poles. This spacing is a deliberate feature of the design, and it keeps the shapes of landmasses locally recognisable. The trade-off is that landmasses far from the Equator appear much larger than they really are, so the amount of exaggeration depends on how far a landmass lies from the Equator. Africa, for example, looks similar in size to Greenland on such a map, even though the two differ greatly in reality. Antarctica is also drawn far larger than its true size. On a standard wall map, India looks like a middleweight beside Scandinavia, which shows how much the grid can change the impression of a country's size. The Equal Earth projection is a newer design, used for thematic maps, that aims to show the whole globe in a more balanced way. Choosing a projection depends on what a map is meant to show, and each design makes its own choices about which features to keep.

questions.q: What was the Mercator projection primarily designed to assist?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Mercator projection was primarily designed to assist maritime navigation.

questions.q: On a Mercator grid, rhumb lines appear as:
questions.explanation: Rhumb lines appear as straight lines on the Mercator grid, which makes it useful for navigation.

questions.q: In reality, Greenland is roughly the size of which country?
questions.explanation: The booklet says that, in reality, Greenland is roughly the size of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Mercator projection preserves the relative area of landmasses.
Reason (R): The stretching of parallels is matched exactly with the stretching of meridians on the Mercator grid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Mercator projection does not preserve relative area, while the exact matching of stretching is a true property of the grid.

questions.q: Which projection type does the Mercator projection belong to?
questions.explanation: The Mercator projection is classified as a cylindrical and conformal projection.

questions.q:
Read the following statements about the Mercator projection:
I. The Mercator projection preserves the relative area of landmasses.
II. Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish geographer and cartographer.
III. Antarctica appears smaller than its true size on the Mercator grid.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement II is correct, since the Mercator projection does not preserve area and Antarctica appears larger than its true size.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about map projections are correct?
I. The Mercator projection has been widely used for centuries.
II. The Mercator projection is an equal-area projection.
III. The Equal Earth projection was designed to display the entire surface of the globe.
IV. The Mercator projection is a compromise projection that balances area, shape, distance and direction.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II and IV contradict the booklet's classification of the Mercator projection.

questions.q: Gerardus Mercator, who introduced the Mercator projection, was a geographer and cartographer from which region? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Mercator as a Flemish geographer and cartographer.

questions.q: How many cartographers created the Equal Earth projection? (in number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Equal Earth was created in 2018 by three cartographers.

questions.q: At what latitude, in degrees North, does the booklet use to show that India is inflated by only about 16% on the Mercator projection? (in degrees)
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that at 22° North the Mercator map inflates India by only about 16%.

questions.q: According to the comparison table, what is the primary advantage of the Equal Earth projection? (three words)
questions.explanation: The comparison table lists accurate relative area as the primary advantage of Equal Earth.

questions.q: Equal Earth is described as an equal-area projection of which type? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Equal Earth as an equal-area, pseudo-cylindrical world map projection.

questions.q: On the comparison table, what is the polar distortion of the Equal Earth projection? (one word)
questions.explanation: The comparison table lists the polar distortion of Equal Earth as reduced, against high for Mercator.

questions.q: According to the comparison table, what is the primary advantage of the Mercator projection? (one word)
questions.explanation: The comparison table lists navigation as the primary advantage of the Mercator projection.

quizzes.title: Other Projections and Mapping in India
quizzes.passage: Map projections are not a single fixed method, and cartographers have produced many of them over time. Every flat map is a trade-off, because a flat sheet cannot match the curved surface of the globe in every respect. The Winkel Tripel was designed to reduce distortion across area, distance and direction together, instead of perfecting one property at the cost of the others. It belongs to a wider group of compromise designs, which spread errors across several properties rather than concentrating them in one. Major institutions, including a large geographic society and the World Bank, later adopted it for their maps. Such compromise maps are used for general reference and world maps, where a natural-looking view of the whole globe is useful. Choosing a projection depends on the purpose of the map, so a design that suits one task may be poor for another. Accuracy matters in official mapping for a different reason. The Survey of India is a national body that works on official maps, and among its tasks is establishing geodetic reference frameworks, which give surveys a common base. The same survey body also checks how international borders appear on published maps. Maps published in India are also subject to legal rules that control how borders may be shown.

questions.q: The Gall-Peters projection was popularised by Arno Peters in which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Arno Peters popularised the Gall-Peters projection in 1973.

questions.q: Which projection is a compromise projection with meridians curving gently towards the Poles?
questions.explanation: The Robinson projection is described as a compromise projection with meridians curving gently towards the Poles.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Robinson projection preserves area exactly.
Reason (R): The Robinson projection was devised by Arthur H. Robinson to balance size and shape.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Robinson is a compromise projection that does not preserve any one property exactly, while its aim to balance size and shape is stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
Read the following statements:
I. The Gall-Peters projection preserves area accurately but makes landmasses look stretched or squashed.
II. The Winkel Tripel projection was created in 1963.
III. The Criminal Law Amendment Act (1961) penalises maps that misrepresent India's borders.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the Winkel Tripel projection is dated to 1921, not 1963.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Gall-Peters projection   ->   A. Oswald Winkel
II. Robinson projection   ->   B. James Gall
III. Winkel Tripel projection   ->   C. Arthur H. Robinson
IV. Survey of India   ->   D. Established in 1767
questions.explanation: James Gall first presented Gall-Peters, Arthur H. Robinson devised Robinson, Oswald Winkel created Winkel Tripel, and the Survey of India was established in 1767.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Survey of India are correct?
I. The Survey of India is headed by the Surveyor General of India.
II. John Mather undertook a modern scientific survey of India.
III. The Survey of India is headed by a Director General.
IV. The Survey of India is headquartered in Bengaluru.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the head is the Surveyor General and the headquarters is not in Bengaluru.

questions.q: Which ministry acts as the nodal agency for the Survey of India?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Ministry of Science and Technology as the nodal agency for the Survey of India.

questions.q: In which year was the Winkel Tripel projection created? (in year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Winkel Tripel projection to 1921.

questions.q: Which section of the Criminal Law Amendment Act (1961) penalises the publication and distribution of certain maps? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Section 2 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act (1961) penalises such maps.

questions.q: In which year was the Gall-Peters projection first presented? (in year)
questions.explanation: James Gall first presented the Gall-Peters projection in 1855, according to the booklet.

questions.q: Arno Peters, who popularised the Gall-Peters projection, was a historian of which nationality? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Arno Peters as a German historian.

questions.q: The Robinson projection was devised partly to solve which problem, named after a landmass? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Robinson projection was devised to balance size and shape and solve the Greenland problem.

questions.q: The Criminal Law Amendment Act (1961) penalises maps that misrepresent India's international borders contrary to what? (two words)
questions.explanation: The Act penalises maps that misrepresent India's international borders contrary to official alignments.

questions.q: In which city is the headquarters of the Survey of India located? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the headquarters of the Survey of India as Dehradun in Uttarakhand.
